notes.name: Named postage-stamp because Phosphor's stamp is the rubber stamp.
notes.drawing: A landscape stamp after the maintainer's reference: a perforated edge, an inner frame and a circle in the middle. The edge is a rectangle (x 32 to 224, y 48 to 208) with shallow circular bites 24 units wide and 10 deep (radius 12.2), five on the long sides and four on the short ones; the round-2 bites (radius 16, a full half circle) were too deep and did not read as a stamp. Six and seven bites a side at depth 8 and 6 were tried: at 16 px they turned into a grey fuzzy border. The inner frame (x 72 to 184, y 88 to 168) keeps 12 units from the bites' inner tips and from the ring (radius 12) in the middle.
notes.bold: Deeper, wider bites (28 wide, 14 deep) so the notches stay open at 24; the frame moves in 4 units (x 76 to 180, y 92 to 164) to keep 6 units from them. The circle is a filled disc of radius 14 with no stroke (a stroked ring would be a 48-unit blob touching the frame; a stroked circle smaller than the half-stroke renders with a hole in the browser).
notes.fill: The stamp is solid; the inner frame and the ring are cut out at regular width.
